raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #59686. `moe_permute` returns wrong `expert_first_token_offset` when `topk_ids` contains `-1` (the id the router writes for CUDA-graph padding tokens with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1`, the default) and no `expert_map` is given. The CUTLASS fp8 MoE path then runs some valid tokens through the wrong expert. This always applies the existing invalid-id remap in `moe_sort_routing`.

## Claims

- Valid tokens' MoE outputs no longer depend on CUDA-graph padding when `CutlassExpertsFp8` (and the other `moe_permute` callers: `cutlass_moe.py` W4A8 path, Humming non-scatter path) run without an `expert_map`.
- Fixes single-request serving quality of fp8 MoE checkpoints on the auto-selected `VLLM_CUTLASS` backend (first-token collapse to `'\n'`, off-topic sampled output).
- No change when all ids are valid or when an `expert_map` is given (the remap already ran there).

## Validation

H100 (SM 9.0), vLLM `main` `47de9d4d04`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt for sm_90 with CUDA 13.1; unpatched = the precompiled nightly extension for the same source.

| check | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| repro from #59686: batch sizes (1..48, padded to a multiple of 8) with wrong offsets | 42 / 48 | 0 / 48 |
| `CutlassExpertsFp8` (E=128, top-4, K=3072, N=1536, per-token act / per-channel weight fp8): sizes where valid rows differ from an unpadded call | 25 / 48 | 0 / 48 |
| new `test_moe_permute_invalid_expert_ids_without_expert_map` | 8 failed (offset assertion) | 8 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py` | | 462 passed |

Model evaluation, 128-expert top-4 fp8 MoE checkpoint (compressed-tensors `FP8_DYNAMIC`), TP=2, default backends (`VLLM_CUTLASS` MoE, CUDA graphs on). Next-token distributions vs. the bf16 checkpoint on 90 short chat prompts x thinking on/off; "foreign mass" = probability the fp8 model puts on its top-10 tokens that are outside the bf16 top-100 (0 for bf16 vs. itself).

| regime (first 8 response tokens) | unpatched: foreign mass / p99 / top-1 agreement | patched |
|---|---|---|
| greedy decode, one request at a time | 0.0081 / 0.39 / 0.951 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.988 |
| teacher-forced, one request at a time | 0.0028 / 0.0000 / 0.979 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.989 |
| teacher-forced, all requests in one batch | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.990 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.990 |

Commands:

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py
```

## Details

Root cause: `CubKeyValueSorter` radix-sorts only the low `floor(log2(2E-1)) + 1` bits, so a raw `-1` (all ones) sorts after every real expert, but `findTotalEltsLessThanTarget` binary-searches the keys as signed ascending ints. Probes landing in the trailing `-1`s push offsets too high, so an expert's grouped-GEMM segment can cover the next expert's rows; when padding outnumbers valid tokens every offset equals the total route count and the valid MoE output is zero. `preprocessTopkIdKernel` already maps ids outside `[0, n_expert)` to the `n_expert` sentinel the sort expects, but it only ran with an `expert_map` or `build_inverse`; `moe_permute` / `moe_permute_with_scratch` pass neither on a single EP rank.

Cost: one `n_token * topk` int32 copy and one elementwise kernel per `moe_permute` call, no host sync, CUDA-graph safe.

`preprocessTopkIdLauncher` now returns early for an empty batch, since the unconditional call would otherwise compute `block = 0`. This overlaps #58790 (empty routing in `moe_permute`, open); whichever lands second can drop its guard.

Not duplicate: open PRs on the same `-1` padding sentinel target other backends (AITER #57036, FlashInfer b12x #57946, XPU #55231) or empty routing (#58790); none changes the `moe_sort_routing` remap gate. Searched `moe_permute`, `expert_first_token_offset`, `topk_ids -1 padding`, `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`, `preprocessTopkId`.

Limitations: validated on H100 only; the sm_90 kernel build used CUDA 13.1.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to localize the bug, write the repros, the fix and the test, and run the validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the results.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

`run_cutlass_moe_fp8` does not clear `mm1_out` on this no-expert-map path. After this remap, padding rows are left unwritten, but dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization still includes them when computing the scale. Stale workspace data can therefore corrupt valid outputs. Please zero or mask these rows and add a padded per-tensor FP8 regression test.

Good catch, thanks. Remapping -1 routes past the valid rows means `run_cutlass_moe_fp8` never writes
those rows of `mm1_out`, but with per-tensor dynamic activation quant (`per_act_token=False`) the
`act_out` scale reduces over the whole workspace, so stale data could skew the scale for valid
tokens.

The existing `mm1_out.fill_(0)` already covered exactly this case for expert-parallel/batched
runs (guarded by `expert_map is not None or use_batched_format`). I'm now applying it whenever the scale is
per-tensor. I added the same guard to `run_cutlass_moe_w4a8_fp8`, which has the same structure. The
per-token path doesn't reduce across rows and is unchanged. The fill is one memset of the `M*topk x 2N` workspace
and only runs on the per-tensor path.

`fused_humming_moe` had the same assumption in its scatter branch: `num_valid_tokens` was only
passed with an expert map. It now always comes from `expert_offsets[-1:]`.

New regression test: `test_run_cutlass_moe_fp8_padded_routes_per_tensor` in
`tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py`. It runs with half the tokens routed to -1, a garbage-filled
workspace and `a2_scale=None`, and compares the valid rows against an unpadded run. It fails
without the fill and passes with it on GB200 (SM100); without the fill the
output is NaN. The existing `test_run_cutlass_moe_fp8` cases and `test_moe_permute_unpermute.py`
(462 cases) still pass.
There's an `assert per_act_token` above at the beginning of this function, so this fill should be unnecessary.  Although, I guess it doesn't hurt.

@@ -1114,3 +1114,95 @@ def test_run_cutlass_moe_fp8(
         torch.testing.assert_close(
             output_random_workspace, output_zero_workspace, atol=5e-3, rtol=1e-3
         )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("per_out_channel", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    (lambda x: x is None or not ops.cutlass_group_gemm_supported(x.to_int()))(
+        current_platform.get_device_capability()
+    ),
+    reason="Grouped gemm is not supported on this GPU type.",
+)
+def test_run_cutlass_moe_fp8_padded_routes_per_tensor(
+    per_out_channel: bool,
+    workspace_init,
+):
+    """Invalid routes without an expert_map must not skew the dynamic
+    per-tensor activation scale.
+
+    The -1 routes of padding tokens sort past the valid rows, so their mm1_out
+    rows are never written by the grouped GEMM. Stale workspace data there must
+    not leak into the per-tensor scale used to quantize act_out.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(7)
+    per_act_token = False
+    num_valid, num_tokens, topk = 16, 32, 2
+    n, k, e = 256, 512, 8
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        mt = MOETensors8Bit.make_moe_tensors_8bit(
+            num_tokens, k, n, e, per_act_token, per_out_channel
+        )
+        # Zero the padding tokens so the input's per-tensor scale is the same
+        # with and without them; only the intermediate scale is under test.
+        hidden_states = mt.a.clone()
+        hidden_states[num_valid:] = 0
+
+        score = torch.randn((num_tokens, e), device="cuda", dtype=torch.half)
+        topk_weights, topk_ids, _ = fused_topk(
+            hidden_states, score, topk, renormalize=False
+        )
+        topk_ids[num_valid:] = -1
+        topk_weights[num_valid:] = 0
+
+        ab_strides1 = torch.full((e,), k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+        ab_strides2 = torch.full((e,), n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+        c_strides1 = torch.full((e,), 2 * n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+        c_strides2 = torch.full((e,), k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+
+        def run(m: int, randomize_workspace: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+            a1q, a1q_scale = moe_kernel_quantize_input(
+                hidden_states[:m], None, torch.float8_e4m3fn, per_act_token
+            )
+            workspace13 = torch.zeros(
+                m * topk * max(2 * n, k), device="cuda", dtype=mt.a.dtype
+            )
+            workspace2 = torch.zeros(
+                m * topk * max(n, k), device="cuda", dtype=mt.a.dtype
+            )
+            if randomize_workspace:
+                workspace13.random_()
+                workspace2.random_()
+            output = torch.zeros((m, k), device="cuda", dtype=mt.a.dtype)
+            run_cutlass_moe_fp8(
+                output,
+                a1q,
+                mt.w1_q,
+                mt.w2_q,
+                topk_ids[:m],
+                MoEActivation.SILU,
+                e,
+                None,  # no expert_map
+                mt.w1_scale,
+                mt.w2_scale,
+                a1q_scale,
+                None,  # dynamic a2 scale
+                ab_strides1,
+                ab_strides2,
+                c_strides1,
+                c_strides2,
+                workspace13,
+                workspace2,
+                None,
+                mt.a.dtype,
+                per_act_token,
+                per_out_channel,
+                False,
+                topk_weights[:m],
+                None,
+            )
+            return output
+
+        expected = run(num_valid, randomize_workspace=False)
+        assert expected.abs().max() > 0
+        actual = run(num_tokens, randomize_workspace=True)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[:num_valid], expected, atol=5e-3, rtol=1e-3)

     )

+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n_expert", [16, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n_valid,n_pad", [(1, 7), (27, 5)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_scratch", [False, True])
+def test_moe_permute_invalid_expert_ids_without_expert_map(
+    n_expert: int, n_valid: int, n_pad: int, use_scratch: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Padding routes (topk_ids == -1) must not shift the expert offsets of
+    valid routes when no expert_map is given."""
+    if not moe_permute_unpermute_supported():
+        pytest.skip("moe_permute_unpermute is not supported on this platform.")
+
+    topk, n_hidden = 4, 256
+    n_token = n_valid + n_pad
+    # Column 0 holds the token index (exact in bf16) to identify permuted rows.
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(n_token, n_hidden, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    hidden_states[:, 0] = torch.arange(n_token, device="cuda")
+    valid_ids = torch.stack(
+        [torch.randperm(n_expert, device="cuda")[:topk] for _ in range(n_valid)]
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    padding = torch.full((n_pad, topk), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    topk_ids = torch.cat([valid_ids, padding])
+
+    scratch = None
+    if use_scratch:
+        scratch = MoEPermuteScratch(
+            num_experts=n_expert,
+            num_local_experts=n_expert,
+            device=hidden_states.device,
+        )
+    permuted, _, expert_offsets, _, _ = moe_permute(
+        hidden_states=hidden_states,
+        a1q_scale=None,
+        topk_ids=topk_ids,
+        n_expert=n_expert,
+        scratch=scratch,
+    )
+
+    counts = torch.bincount(valid_ids.flatten(), minlength=n_expert)
+    expected_offsets = torch.cat([counts.new_zeros(1), counts.cumsum(0)])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(expert_offsets, expected_offsets)
+
+    # Each expert segment holds exactly the tokens routed to that expert.
+    for e in torch.nonzero(counts).flatten().tolist():
+        lo, hi = expert_offsets[e].item(), expert_offsets[e + 1].item()
+        actual = permuted[lo:hi, 0].long().sort().values
+        expected = (valid_ids == e).any(dim=1).nonzero().flatten()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
